answers.explanation: Parts, how they relate, and what the whole is for.
Staff, admins, and users are parts of the system, and so are their mistakes.
Interconnections: how the elements relate. They're often the least protected part.
We patch the boxes and forget what happens when a trusted link between them is abused.
It's a procedure question: processes protect functions and interconnections.
Coordinating with outside groups mobilizes knowledge you don't have yourself.
Segmentation limits how far an incident spreads. You'll see micro-segmentation in the network lesson.
Insiders use real, legitimate interconnections. That's what makes collusion and espionage so hard to spot.
Traceability, alongside trust modeling, is one way to make interconnections more resilient.
